sentiment.label: neutral
sentiment.reason_it: I mercati azionari hanno chiuso la scorsa settimana con un tono positivo, S&P 500 +1.08%, mentre il VIX è sceso significativamente (-11.06%) a 16.40. Il DXY è salito (+0.76%) a 100.85, segno di una certa avversione al rischio. L'oro è sceso (-1.21%) a $4172.90/oz. I dati macro recenti (CPI, Core CPI, Non-Farm Payrolls) sono stati in linea con le attese, non generando grosse sorprese. La BCE ha mantenuto i tassi invariati al 2.00% (DFR) e 2.15% (Refi).
sentiment.reason_en: The equity markets ended last week on a positive note, S&P 500 +1.08%, while VIX significantly decreased (-11.06%) to 16.40. The DXY rose (+0.76%) to 100.85, indicating some risk aversion. Gold declined (-1.21%) to $4172.90/oz. Recent macro data (CPI, Core CPI, Non-Farm Payrolls) were in line with expectations, not generating significant surprises. ECB kept rates unchanged at 2.00% (DFR) and 2.15% (Refi).

market_impact_summary.it: Nella chiusura della scorsa settimana, S&P 500 +1.08%, DXY +0.76%, VIX -11.06%. TLT +0.49%, US 10Y Yield -0.27%. L'oro è sceso (-1.21%) a $4172.90/oz, mentre il petrolio è salito (+0.93%) a $80.59. I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso con risultati misti: Nikkei +0.28%, Shanghai -0.43%, Hang Seng -1.59%.
market_impact_summary.en: In last week's close, S&P 500 +1.08%, DXY +0.76%, VIX -11.06%. TLT +0.49%, US 10Y Yield -0.27%. Gold declined (-1.21%) to $4172.90/oz, while oil rose (+0.93%) to $80.59. Asian markets closed mixed: Nikkei +0.28%, Shanghai -0.43%, Hang Seng -1.59%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.


Mentre i mercati tradizionali sono chiusi per il fine settimana, riassumiamo la chiusura precedente. 
Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.28%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.43% e l'Hang Seng in calo dell'1.59%.


Sul fronte occidentale, nella seduta di venerdì, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dell'1.08%, il VIX in calo dell'11.06%. 
Il dollaro si è rafforzato, con il DXY in aumento dello 0.76% e l'EUR/USD in calo dello 0.09% a 1.14
L'oro ha chiuso in calo dell'1.21% a $4172.9/oncia, il petrolio in rialzo dello 0.93% a $80.59


Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.


Tra le notizie, l'attenzione si concentra sulle implicazioni geopolitiche e sui piani di finanziamento dell'UE, 
con particolare attenzione alla crisi in Iran e alle tensioni commerciali.


Restiamo in attesa per l'apertura dei mercati nella prossima settimana.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i sessantatremila dollari, con una variazione del +0,80% nella giornata. I flussi ETF hanno registrato una saída di 90,7 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle tensioni geopolitiche, con una rinnovata minaccia nello stretto di Hormuz che potrebbe incidere sui colloqui di cessate il fuoco tra Stati Uniti e Iran. 
  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum guadagna lo 0,32% a mille settecento ventotto dollari, mentre Solana registra un +3,05% a settantatre virgola quarantasei dollari. BNB in leggero aumento dello 0,47% a cinquecentottantotto virgola quarantadue dollari. 
  Il sentiment del mercato, misurato dall'indice Fear & Greed, è a 23, in zona di Extreme Fear, il che suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 

While traditional markets are closed for the weekend, let's recap the previous close. 
The Nikkei closed up 0.28%, Shanghai down 0.43%, and the Hang Seng down 1.59%.

On the Western front, on Friday, the S&P 500 closed up 1.08%, the VIX down 11.06%. 
The dollar strengthened, with the DXY up 0.76% and the EUR/USD down 0.09% to 1.14
Gold closed down 1.21% at $4172.9/oz, oil up 0.93% at $80.59

No major macroeconomic data out today.

Among the news, attention is focused on geopolitical implications and EU financing plans, 
with particular attention to the Iran crisis and trade tensions.

We're looking forward to the market opening next week.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin holds above sixty-three thousand dollars, with a change of +0.8% today. ETF flows recorded an outflow of $90.7 million. This movement could be influenced by geopolitical tensions, with a renewed threat in the Strait of Hormuz that could impact US-Iran ceasefire talks. 
Among altcoins, Ethereum gains 0.32% to $1728, while Solana registers a +3.05% to $73.46 BNB up slightly by 0.47% to $588.42 
The market sentiment, measured by the Fear & Greed index, is at 23, in Extreme Fear territory, suggesting investor caution.

No macro data on the agenda today. To dive deeper into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thanks for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: A Budget for Global Turmoil: Peace, Conflict and the EU’s Funding Plans

articles.title: Geopolitics and global value chains: Implications for trade policy and development in Asia
articles.snippet: Rising geopolitical tensions and increasing fragmentation introduce new risks into global production networks, forcing both disruptions and creating new strategic opportunities. How is US trade policy shaping these tensions and how are developing Asia-Pacific participants responding to them? This session provides an overview of how the content of global supply chains have been reshaped by US protectionism, how developing countries can engage and upgrade, and the turbulence expected over the coming year. articles.title: Petrol prices in Australia are now lower than before the Iran war began. Is the oil crisis over and what happens next?
articles.snippet: Fuel suppliers outside the Middle East have proved to be much more flexible than analysts expected – and China surprised everyone Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australians were warned soon after the Middle East conflict started that the country could run short on fuel, with prices rising to record levels owing to disrupted oil supplies. Now, amid an uneasy peace deal and continued supply disruptions, petrol prices are lower than they were before the conflict began and official warnings over fuel usage have largely disappeared.
